Specify age-specific demographic rates

Source: R/set_process.R
mortality.Rd

Construct a process specification without running a simulation. Rates are piecewise constant over age intervals [age_start, age_end), in years, and expressed per person-year. Overlapping intervals are rejected; adjacent intervals are allowed. Input order and custom columns are preserved; rate schedules are returned as tibbles. A source attribute on the input table is copied to the process's source field.

Usage

mortality(rates, group_prop_hazard = NULL)

fertility(
  rates,
  birth_interval = 0.75,
  group_prop_hazard = NULL,
  inheritance = create_group_inheritance(),
  ffab = 0.4886,
  hetfert = NULL
)

Arguments

rates

A nonempty data frame containing numeric age_start, age_end, and rate. Starts must be finite and nonnegative; ends must exceed starts and may be Inf for upper-open bands. Rates must be finite and nonnegative. Mortality additionally requires character sex values "m" and "f", with both represented.

group_prop_hazard

Optional named numeric vector of finite nonnegative rate multipliers, with unique nonempty group names. Missing groups use 1.0; zero suppresses the risk. Values are not normalized. At execution, multiply the selected input schedule by the person's group factor, including all sex/status strata. Fertility multiplication precedes cell accounting. Without population groups, warn and ignore multipliers. Stored rate tables and their source metadata are unchanged; rate-table summaries use those stored rates, without applying population-dependent multipliers. Fertility with union_type rates also accepts a named list such as list(partnered = c(A = 1.1, B = 0.9), unpartnered = c(A = 1.05)). An omitted status or group uses 1.0. A single vector applies to all types (or overall fertility). Type lists require union_type rates and their names must match the supplied schedule types. Three-type schedules accept lists named unpartnered/cohab/marriage; shared partnered schedules accept unpartnered/partnered. Omitted types and groups have multiplier 1.

birth_interval

Minimum maternal birth-to-birth interval in years, defaulting to 0.75. Must be finite and nonnegative. Applies to fertility only; see cell-accounted fertility below.

inheritance

A group identity model from create_group_inheritance(), or a tibble with numeric time_start, time_end and list-column model containing complete inheritance models. Intervals are half-open absolute years, must not overlap and must cover the requested run. Select the active model at each birth; older identities and ancestry remain unchanged. Base data frames with list columns are accepted. All declared possible identities across scheduled models join the simulation-wide registry. Static inputs may also be a method name requiring no additional parameters: "mother", "father", "random_parent", "same_sex", "opposite_sex", or "ancestry". Fertility defaults to selecting either parent with equal probability, with maternal fallback. Other parental, ancestry, hierarchy, and custom rules assign identity after child sex and ancestry are calculated. Possible identities are checked against grouped schedules and categorical matching levels before execution. Applies to fertility only.

ffab

Probability that a newborn is female, default 0.4886. Must be a finite numeric scalar in [0, 1]. Applies to fertility only.

hetfert

NULL (default) for uniform mother selection, or a het_fert() specification for persistent lognormal selection weights.

Value

A named list containing name, rates, and rate_unit, plus birth_interval and ffab for fertility, inheriting from hammel_mortality or hammel_fertility and hammel_process.

Details

An optional group column supplies separate schedules by nonmissing character label or finite numeric code. Without it, rates apply to all groups. Each mortality group needs both sexes, and each conditional fertility group needs both statuses. Overlap is checked within groups. Simulation requires schedules for every population group. Without population groups, simulation warns and uses the first group alphabetically (radix order of character representations, including numeric codes).

Mortality requires separate schedules for both sexes. Gaps and uncovered ages are not filled or interpreted as zero rates. Coverage must be specified before simulation. Optional time_start/time_end columns select half-open calendar intervals in absolute years, including fractional years, on mortality and fertility tables. Both columns are required together; starts are finite and ends exceed starts (possibly Inf). Active slices must satisfy the existing strata/coverage rules and cover the requested run. Rates are constant within intervals, with no interpolation. Calendar changes precede same-time events, preserving histories, birth spacing, parity and duration origins. Inheritance also accepts whole-model calendar schedules; other fertility arguments remain static.

Fertility optionally accepts union_type containing both "partnered" and "unpartnered", or all three "unpartnered", "cohab", "marriage". Shared partnered rates cover either partnership type. Rates use woman-years in the indicated type; the old fertility input union_status is rejected. Without that column, one overall schedule applies to all women. A partial status table or any other label is rejected; use explicit zero rates to suppress births in a status. Overlap is checked separately within each status. On-demand union formation requires overall rates; rate-based formation accepts either form and warns when an overall schedule is used.

Optional parity_start/parity_end use half-open current maternal parity bands, covering zero through Inf without gaps or overlap in every group/type stratum. Parity is counted from recorded maternal births (including deceased children) and incremented only on successful births; no custom parity column overrides history. A pooled parity band applies its rate to each contained actual parity.

Birth spacing uses cell-accounted fertility (D101). Women are grouped into cells: one-year (or shorter) age sub-bands of each group/union-type schedule after group multipliers, split at whole ages and band edges, and one actual parity when rates are parity-specific. Each cell produces births at its input rate times all its living members, including those inside the birth interval, and each birth goes to an eligible member, uniformly by default or proportional to persistent weights when hetfert is enabled. Observed rates then equal inputs in expectation for any population composition, including after restarts and union-type changes, while a cell has an eligible member. Intensity in cells with members but none eligible is dropped and reported in simulation$unrealized_births. An individual woman's hazard depends on recent births by others in her cell; this is a calibration device. Upper-open age bands stay one cell when birth_interval * rate is below 0.001 and are otherwise split yearly. Zero-rate bands form no cells.

For parity-specific schedules with a positive birth_interval, fertility() warns when positive rates fall in one-year age cells where no woman can be eligible: births are singletons at least birth_interval apart, starting from the schedule's first positive rate, so parity k is first eligible at the age found by following each parity's first positive rate. Union types are pooled and groups checked separately. Partly reachable cells and higher actual parities within an open parity band (always unreachable at the youngest ages) are not reported.

Examples

deaths <- mortality(data.frame(sex = c("m", "f"), age_start = 0,
  age_end = Inf, rate = c(0.01, 0.008)))
births <- fertility(data.frame(age_start = 15, age_end = 50, rate = 0.1))
model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_process(deaths) |>
  set_process(births)
